LNU MANDATE AND BRIEF History Our Mandate The LEYTE NORMAL UNIVERSITY, a government institution of higher learning established under R.A. 7910 in 1995, is mandated to: A. Primarily provide higher professional and special instructions for special purposes and promote research and extension services, advanced studies and progressive leadership in education and other related fields as may be relevant. B. Offer undergraduate and graduate courses in the fields of education and other related degree courses as the Board of Regents may deem necessary to carry out its objectives. LNU: A Brief History The history of Leyte Normal University dates back to 1921 when it came into being as the provincial Normal School, an adjunct of the Leyte High School, with a mandate to train teachers for elementary teaching. It eventually outgrew its base, becoming a two - year collegiate training institution in 1938 independent of the Leyte High School, offering only the Elementary Teaching Certificate (ETC). Known as the Leyte Normal School, it became a degree - granting four - year college complete with a training department in 1952. Then on June 14, 1976, it was converted into the Leyte State College when the late President Ferdinand E. Marcos signed Presidential Decree No. 944, authorizing the college to operate under its own charter. The late Congressman of the First District of Leyte, Hon. Cirilo Roy Montejo, recognizing the strength and capability of the institution, filed House Bill No. 22 proposing the conversion of Leyte State College into a university. Co - sponsored in the Senate by the Chairman of the Education Committee, the late Hon. Letecia Ramos - Shahani, House Bill No. 22 was enacted into law under Republic Act No. 7901 finally converting the Leyte State College into Leyte Normal University on February 23, 1995. II. II, Section 1). 1. VISION A globally recognized university of education, management, arts and sciences geared towards the inclusive growth and sustainability of society

GOALS / OBJECTIVES To realize its Mission/Vision, Leyte Normal University is committed to the following institutional objectives: 3.1 To upgrade and maintain its standards as a Center of Excellence within the limits of its resources; 3.2 To provide an environment conducive to serious study and research as well as tolerance, openness, and respect for the ideas and opinions of others; and 3.3 To develop God - centered, nationalistic, values - oriented, and productive students capable of participating actively, competitively, and constructively in national and global needs, issues, and concerns. 4. CORE VALUES 4.1 Integrity We are accountable, honest, trustworthy, respectful, and ethical in our actions We upload a level of independence that assures confidence 4.2 Excellence We persistently pursue success and continuously look for innovative ways to improve our services. 4.3 Service We serve our internal and external customers with a smile We deliver outstanding service to all, regardless of status, creed, color, and race III. THE UNIVERSITY GOVERNANCE The administration of the university and the exercise of its corporate power is vested exclusively in its governing body called the Board of Regents and the President of the university insofar as authorized by pertinent laws. The Board promulgates and implements policies in accordance with the declared state policies on the education of the 1987 Philippine Constitution and other pertinent provisions on education, science, and technology, arts, culture, and sports,; as well as the policies, standards, and thrusts of the CHED under Republic Act No. 7722.

Two (2) prominent citizens who have distinguished themselves in their professions or fields of specialization chosen from among the list of at least five (5) persons qualified in the city or the province. who shall render full - time service. The President carries out the general policies laid down by the Board of Regents and has general supervision of all business and financial operations of the university. The President is assisted by a Vice President for Academic ServicesAffairs, a Vice President for Administration and Finance, Vice President for Research, and Innovation, and Extension, and a Vice President for Student Development. The President is assisted further by a Management Committee composed of the Vice Presidents, Deans, and Chief Administrative Officer, whose primary function is to assist and support advise the University President on Academic and Administrative matters. There are Academic Administrators designated by the University President and confirmed by the LNU Board who assist the President. They are as follows: Academic Deans, Academic Department Chairs, Directors of Research, Innovation, Planning, and Community Extension Services, Planning Officer, International Affairs & Linkages, Integrated Laboratory School, Community Extension Services, Learning Resource Center, Management Information System, Income Generating Projects, Cultural Affairs, and Special Projects, Continuing Education & Lifelong Learning Review Centers, Quality Management System and Accreditation, and ETEEAP, Board and University Secretary , and LNU House Manager. and unit program chairs. | Student Handbook 2022 Edition 6 | Student Handbook 2022 Edition I. ADMISSION SERVICES 1. Registration and Document Services The Office of the Registrar is the repository of academic records. It offers services academic/scholastic records. It serves the currently enrolled students, alumni, and those who left the University without finishing a degree. Primary services are registration, records management, student evaluation, and document services. 1.1 Registration Registration is the process that provides the student with an official capacity in the University. A student is assigned his/her assigned ID number prior to registration and upon confirmation of his/her slot for admission. Every student performs a manual or regular registration. This requires students to be on campus and to line up during registration. Registration by proxy or representative will be allowed during registration proper with the following requirements to be presented: 1.1.1 LNU ID or any ID with the picture and signature of the student being proxied. 1.1.2 Typewritten or word - processed Authorization Letter 2. Records Management Records management is the efficient and timely implementation of a systematic process for recording, maintaining/updating, monitoring, evaluating, releasing, and safekeeping of student records. Students must ensure that their records are complete and deposited at the Office of the Registrar. Lacking documents will prevent official status in the University and graduation. 3. Student Evaluation Student Evaluation is the process that determines and assesses the credentials and monitors accomplishment a academic requirements to ensure eligibility to enroll in the next semester and graduate. It involves the analysis of the educational history of students, especially those who attended several schools. It also covers the proper sequencing and transfer of credentials and their sufficiency, validity, and authenticity. 4. Document Services Standard document requests include the Diploma, Transcript of Records, and Certifications (i.e., enrolment, graduation, general weighted average, etc.). 4.1 Requirements for Processing/Releasing of Documents: 4.1.1 Official documents will be processed/released to the student upon settlement of all financial, disciplinary, academic, and documentary

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SERVICES The Management Information System (MIS) Office provides IT support to all academic and administrative units in the university. The MIS administers the development, implementation, and maintenance of the academic and administrative information systems, takes care of the and records in the Information System (IS), and ensures the security and maintenance of school records. The Student Information System (SIS) is a web - based information system where the students can view pertinent school information, including their basic information, official curriculum, program of study, grades, class schedules, and the like. Students may view their grades through the MyLNU app, the official mobile application of Leyte Normal University. III. GUIDANCE AND COUNSELLING 1. The Goal of Guidance Services Providing a helping, supportive and facilitative role in the achievement of the mission and goals, the LNU Guidance Services aim to assist every student so that he/she may: 1.1 Gain an understanding of himself/herself and others; 1.2 Become self - directed and self - reliant to the end that he/she can make necessary adjustments to the school setting and to his/her academic, personal, and social life; 1.3 Acquire desirable values, and 1.4 Conceive realistic plans for his/her future life after leaving school. 2. The Guidance Services available to students include the following: 2.1 Orientation This provides students information on the historical background of the university, school policies, school rules and regulations, grading system, academic and non - academic scholarships, cultural affairs, student organizations, and other

| Student Handbook 2022 Edition 8 | Student Handbook 2022 Edition basic information. 2.2 Information This service makes available to students various up - to - date, relevant information about the college, other institutions of higher learning, careers in the - personal development. Any of the Guidance staff shall welcome any student who may want to avail of information materials in the Guidance Office or in their collection. 2.3 Counseling This service is the heart of Guidance Services. Counseling aims at helping each student clarify his conflicts, and minimize or solve the problems that block his development as a person. It also assists him in discovering his potential, defining his feelings, and clarifying his motives. Through counseling, students may be expected to understand and accept themselves and seek to grow into better persons who can think independently, make wise decisions, and act responsibly. Students may avail of the counseling service following the schedule (posted outside the counseling room) for counseling, by making an appointment with a counselor, or by dropping in immediately whenever there is a need for the service and a counselor is available, thru self - referral. Referrals may also be made by any university instructors/professors. 2.4 Peer Counseling Students trained in certain counseling skills (called Peer Counselors) assist fellow students with problems. The Peer Counselors also serve as the bridge between the counselor and students who need help in resolving academic, personal, and social adjustment problems. To render optimal service to fellow students, peer counselors may hold small group sessions or meetings to give help so as to attract students to avail of their services. Peer counselors are always available every day because they follow a daily schedule (posted outside the Guidance Office). 2.5 Testing This service assists students in discovering their mental capacities, personality needs, study habits and attitudes, interests and aptitudes. The accurate interpretation of test results and the appropriate communication of the same will enable students to make realistic plans about their college and future life. Standardized tests may be administered for instructional purposes (as requested by the Deans or other units), and the test administration will be scheduled by course and year - level. However, individual or small groups of students may avail of the services for diagnostic or counseling purposes by completing a request form and submitting the same to the Guidance Services Office.

STUDENT HOUSING / DORMITORY The privilege of living in the dormitory is given to students on a first come - first served basis. It is expected that being housed in the dormitory would help the residents develop values that foster wholesome community living, ; respect for law and order, wise management of time and resources, ability to engage in healthful vocational pursuits, habits of sanitation, and mental hygiene. Thus all dormitory residents are expected at all times and on all occasions to conduct themselves appropriately. Available rooms may be reserved for performing art groups, School Publication Staff, and SSC Officers, for an overnight stay due to school - related activities. Dormitory admission is semestral. Students who want to stay at the dormitory may apply to the Dormitory Manager. The qualified dormitory occupants shall be advised to pay the dorm application fee equivalent to a one - month deposit and one - month advance (P1,600.00) at the office upon enrollment. Prior to the admittance to the dormitory, the resident is required to submit the following: Two copies of X colored ID pictures taken not more than six months ago Entrance slip The remaining amount for the entire semester will be paid during the midterm (P2,400). If a resident decides to terminate the contract before midterm, he/she shall be charged 50% of the remaining amount for the entire semester after which he/she will be issued a dormitory clearance. The dorm advisers may recommend to the administration to refuse admission/expulsion of the students on the basis of inappropriate behavior.

It is an accepted fact that students learn better and faster when they are healthy. Cognizant of this direct relationship, the school makes is an active leader in promoting protecting, and maintening of good health. 1. Scope of Work of the Clinic 1.1 Render routine health examinations to the school population. This is done by schedule. 1.2 Provide medical consultation and treatment of minor ailments and emergency cases. 1.3 Make appropriate referrals and follow up when necessary. 1.4 Determine the physical and mental fitness of the school population who will participate in physical education programs, athletic competitions, pre - military, and other related activities. 1.5 Provide health examination of school personnel to certify maternity and/or sick leave as well as readmission to or exclusion from classes. 1.6 Take leadership in establishing a functional school clinic and providing technical supervision in its maintenance. 1.7 Help in the administration and the sanitation of school plants. 1.8 Render oral (mouth) examination to all first - year college students. 1.9 Conduct oral prophylaxis and tooth filling to prevent and control dental decay. 1.10 Students are entitled to one free dental service for either: tooth extraction, tooth filing, and oral prophylaxis. 1.11 All dental services are accommodated on an appointment basis only, except for emergency cases. 2. How to Avail of the Medical Services 2.1 The physician and the nurse man the Medical Section. Clinic hours are Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., and Saturdays and Sundays 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., for Graduate School students. 2.2 Initial assessment is done by the school nurse and the medical record of the patient will be retrieved from the record files. 2.3 Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, height in cm., and weights in kg.), when needed will be recorded by the nurse. 2.4 The school physician examines the patient and will be managed accordingly. Emergency medicines are available at the clinic, and the patient will be given the initial dose/s for free. Subsequent doses needed to complete the treatment will be prescribed by the physician. 2.5 There are health conditions wherein the patients need to be referred to diagnostic laboratories and/or hospitals. They should return to the clinic for evaluation of the

No medical certificate will be issued if there is no check - up done at the clinic. For consultations made outside, the medical certificate of the attending physician will be countersigned by the school physician, and this will be noted in the medical record files. 2.7 Entry slips (issued by the physician) to be presented to the security guard will be given to students who cannot wear the prescribed shoes due to some foot ailments. 2.8 Routine health examination is done to the incoming first - year, practicum students, and new students/transferees/returnees prior to enrollment, athletes in preparation for athletic meets, scholarship applicants, and the rest of the school populace as scheduled. 3. How to Avail of the Dental Services 3.1 The dentist and the dental aide man the Dental section. Clinic hours are Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and Sundays at 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 1:00 to 5:00 p.m. for Graduate School students. 3.2 The dental aide retrieves the dental record of the patient from the record files. 3.3 Emergency dental problems, such as toothache, swollen gums due to the various tooth, and other dental emergencies, are attended to anytime during clinic hours. 3.4 Each student/ILS pupil can avail of one of the following dental procedures per semester: dental extraction, dental filling, and oral prophylaxis. 3.5 To avail of the above - mentioned services, the students need to see the dentist for scheduling every 12:00 p.m. to 1:00 p.m., Monday to Friday. 3.6 The patients are given an initial dose of their medicines for free; the rest need to complete the treatment will be prescribed by the school dentist. 3.7 Routine dental examination to incoming first - year and practicum students and new studentsis done prior to enrollment, and the rest of the school populace as scheduled. 3.8 ILS pupils should be accompanied by the parent/guardian during a dental procedure. VII. FOOD SERVICES The LNU House Food and Beverage Area and the LNU Cafeteria are self - sustaining units of the university that provide food services. All its operational expenses are derived from the minimal profit from the food services activity. Its main objectives/functions are to serve nutritious but low - cost meals and snacks to the school populace and to be a laboratory for the Bachelor of Science in Entrepreneurship and the Home Economics students enrolled in food preparation and cafeteria management courses.

Aside from the LNU Cafeteria, the LNU IGP Food Park and the Coop Canteen also serve affordable meals and snacks from Monday to Friday and during weekends when there are classes at the Graduate School. Students are also expected to observe the above - mentioned policies at the IGP Food Park and the Coop Canteen. VIII. LIBRARY SERVICES The user must have a working knowledge of some of its organizational aspects to get the maximum benefit from the LNU Learning Resource Center or any library. The LNU LRC is automated. To allow maximum benefits, students are encouraged to spend quality time at the Learning Resource Center. There are trained Student Aides to help other students find their way in the LRC. Efficient and effective utilization of the library includes some behavioral considerations. Students are therefore required to know and follow library rules and regulations. These are emphasized in orientation sessions, but the details are posted at the entrance of the library. The relationship between the library and its clientele is a two - way affair. For students to expand or increase their knowledge, they are also obliged to help preserve its materials, promote smooth social relationships among library staff and other users, and maintain that kind of library atmosphere conducive to study and research.

THE UNIVERSITY MUSEUM The Leyte Normal University Museum is an institution established to commemorate the centennial anniversary of the university in the year 2021. It aims to provide learning by disseminating knowledge of the university in terms of its cultural and historical heritage. Notably, it collects and exhibits its memorabilia and photographic collection that dating back to 1917. It archives important documents and promotes the aesthetic presentation of various artifacts. The interim exhibit of the LNU Museum is housed in Brillo Hall, one of the oldest buildings in the university whose historical significance deservedly finds its place as an institution of historicity. VI. ADMINISTRATIVE DUE PROCESS A student charged with violating school rules and regulations is entitled to administrative due process. For LIGHT OFFENSES, the VPSD or, in his absence, the duly designated hearing officer, is authorized to receive the evidence and on the bases thereof, render his decision, which is final and executory. For SERIOUS and VERY SERIOUS OFFENSES, the Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) shall hear and try the case and impose the sanctions provided therein. 1. Filing of Charges Disciplinary proceedings commence upon the filing of a written charge of any violation of existing rules and regulations (Disciplinary Referral Slip or Disciplinary Action Slip) by any security officer, faculty or personnel at the Office of Student Affairs. The case shall be entered in the official entry book kept for the purpose, specifying the person/persons charged, his/her witness, the date of filing, and the substance of the charge. The university shall not take any complaint with regard ordinary debts of students with private parties, except when the case involves the moral character of the students.

Preliminary Inquiry Upon receipt of the complaint, the Preliminary Hearing Committee composed of the VPSD, Adviser or Unit Chair of the student/s concerned, SSC Adviser, and a guidance office shall determine if such complaint or report is sufficient to warrant formal investigation. In cases where the complaint or report is found sufficient, formal charges shall be filed and served upon each respondent and his/her parent or guardian. 3. Answer The respondent should answer in writing within ten (10) calendar days from receipt of the charges. If there is no reply, the formal investigation shall be held. 4 Notice of Hearing The Chair of the SDC, which is the dean of the respondent, shall notify the student as well as his/her parents/guardians regarding the date and venue of the formal hearing. In cases when the complainant is another student, the parents or guardians of both the complainant and the respondent must be notified and must be present during the hearing. 5. Formal Hearing/Investigation The initial hearing shall be not less than five (5) nor more than ten (10) working days after receipt of written notice of all parties. When either of the parties has filed charges in court, the SDC may suspend the disciplinary hearing and shall not intervene in the court proceedings. 6. Finality of the Decision The SDC shall endeavor to render its decision by majority vote within fifteen days after it receives the complaint. Its decision is final and executory, except when a penalty of SUSPENSION or EXPULSION is imposed, in which case such decision shall be reviewed by MANCOM. 7. Appeal to the President An appeal may be made directly to the University President if the sanction is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, the appeal should be elevated to the Board of Regents (BOR) for review. 8. Decision of the Board of Regents The Board shall review the decision of the University President when the penalty imposed is expulsion, suspension for more than five (5) days, or any penalty of equivalent severity, and render final judgment thereof.
